subject: biology
title: The endocrine system
key_idea: Endocrine glands release hormones directly into the blood. The blood carries each hormone to its target organ, where it has an effect. Compared with the nervous system, the effects are slower but last longer.

blocks.text: The endocrine system is made of glands. This section covers what they release and how the message reaches the body.

items.meaning: A gland that releases hormones directly into the bloodstream.
A chemical messenger that is carried in the blood and changes how a target organ works.
The organ or cells that a hormone acts on.

items.text: A gland secretes a hormone into the bloodstream.
The hormone is carried in the blood plasma around the body.
It reaches its target organ, binds to receptors on the cells and produces an effect.

items: The **pituitary gland** in the brain is the "master gland". It secretes several hormones into the blood in response to body conditions.
Some pituitary hormones act on other glands and stimulate them to release their own hormones.
Glands release hormones into the blood. The blood carries them to the target organ.
The pituitary is the master gland because its hormones control other glands.

parts.name: Pituitary gland
parts.detail: In the head, attached to the brain. Releases several hormones, including ADH, FSH and LH, and so controls other glands.

parts.name: Thyroid gland
parts.detail: In the neck. Releases thyroxine, which increases the metabolic rate. More is released when body temperature falls.

parts.name: Pancreas
parts.detail: In the abdomen. Releases insulin and glucagon, which control blood glucose. Their target organs include the liver and muscles.

parts.name: Adrenal glands
parts.detail: In the abdomen. Release adrenaline, which increases heart rate and breathing rate and delivers more oxygen and glucose to cells.

parts.name: Ovaries
parts.detail: Glands involved in human reproduction in females. LH from the pituitary gland acts on the ovary.

parts.name: Testes
parts.detail: Glands involved in human reproduction in males.

items: **Thyroxine** increases the metabolic rate. Respiration then releases more heat, so body temperature rises.
**Adrenaline** increases heart rate. More oxygen and glucose reach the brain and muscles for respiration, which releases the energy for movement.
Know the glands: pituitary, thyroid, pancreas, adrenal, ovary and testis.
Each hormone acts only on its target organs.

blocks.text: The body uses two coordination systems. Hormones and nerves differ in how they send messages.

items: Endocrine: chemical, in the blood, slower, longer-lasting.
Nervous: electrical, along neurones, faster, shorter.

checks.q: Which gland is called the master gland, and why?
checks.a: The pituitary gland. It secretes several hormones that act on other glands to stimulate them to release hormones.

checks.q: How is a hormone carried from its gland to its target organ?
checks.a: It is carried in the blood, dissolved in the plasma.

checks.q: Give two ways that coordination by the endocrine system differs from coordination by the nervous system.
checks.a: Any two from: slower; longer-lasting; chemical hormones carried in the blood instead of electrical impulses along neurones.

exam_phrases: (chemical / hormone) via blood instead of electrical / impulse / neurones
target organs for insulin are the liver and muscle

mistakes.right: Answers must be comparative. Say that it is slower, longer-lasting, or uses hormones in the blood instead of electrical impulses along neurones.

mistakes.wrong: The endocrine system sends hormones to target organs.
mistakes.right: "Hormones" and "target organs" alone are ignored. Give a real difference, such as chemical transmission, slower or longer-lasting.

mistakes.wrong: Thyroxine increases respiration, which produces energy to warm the body.
mistakes.right: "Energy produced / made / created" is not accepted. Say that respiration releases energy, or releases heat.

worked_example.question:
The endocrine system coordinates many internal functions of the body.

Give three ways coordination by the endocrine system is different from coordination by the nervous system.
answer_points: It uses chemicals (hormones) in the blood instead of electrical impulses along neurones.
Allow the converse points if they clearly refer to nervous coordination.
worked_example.tip: One mark each. Every answer must be a comparison, not just a description of hormones.

exam_phrases: pancreas produces insulin; the target organs are the liver and muscles
the pituitary gland is situated in the head and is attached to the brain
the thyroid gland is part of the endocrine system

mistakes.wrong: Insulin travels to its target organ along neurones, or on red blood cells.
mistakes.right: Hormones do not travel along neurones and do not attach to red blood cells. Say that insulin is dissolved in the blood plasma.

mistakes.wrong: Insulin is produced by the adrenal glands and acts on the intestines.
mistakes.right: The adrenal glands do not produce insulin and the intestines are not its target organs. Insulin is made by the pancreas and acts on the liver and muscles.

worked_example.question:
Insulin is a hormone that controls blood glucose concentration.

State how insulin is transported from its endocrine gland to its target organs.
answer_points: Accept: in the blood system, in blood vessels, in arteries or in veins. Ignore capillaries.
worked_example.tip: A one-mark recall question. Name the blood, not nerves or cells.

exam_phrases: secreted / released from glands / endocrine cells

mistakes.wrong: Hormones are transported in the blood.
mistakes.right: For two marks on how hormones reach their targets, give both points: in the blood / blood vessels, and in the plasma. "In the blood plasma" earns both.

mistakes.wrong: The endocrine system is faster than the nervous system and its effects are short.
mistakes.right: This is the wrong way round. Endocrine is slower acting and longer-lived. The nervous system uses electrical impulses along neurones.

worked_example.question:
Hormones are produced in endocrine glands.

Describe how hormones control different parts of the body.
answer_points: Secreted / released from glands or endocrine cells (allow a named gland).
Affect target organs / cells (allow: hormones bind to specific receptors).
worked_example.tip: Two marks from three points: release from a gland, carried in the blood, and acting on target organs.
